Anthropic released the "Claude 4" family, consisting of two models—Opus 4 and Sonnet 4—on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. This dual-model strategy allowed Anthropic to differentiate its offerings by positioning Opus 4 as the flagship model with a price of $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens, while designating Sonnet 4 as the fast workhorse and developer-default coding model at a lower cost of $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

The launch signaled that agentic coding was becoming the defining product trend of 2025, driven largely by the rise of Claude Code [Source: ev-1]. By emphasizing "computer use 2.0" capabilities that were roughly twice as reliable as the previous 3.x generation, Anthropic positioned itself against competitors like OpenAI's o-series amidst an enterprise agentic-coding gold rush [Source: ev-1]. The company aimed to establish its models as the safest and most reliable coding agents in this market shift [Source: ev-1].
